script.opening_words: Somewhere in America right now, a 28-year-old is opening a lease renewal letter. She's been in this one-bedroom for 2 years. It's fine. The dishwasher works about 70% of the time, and the neighbor above her does what sounds like competitive bowling at 11:00 p.m., but it's home. She scans down to the number. Her rent is going up $185 a month. She does the math in her head fast, the way you get good at when every month is
script.ending_words: a reminder, I'm not a financial advisor. This video is for educational purposes only. If this one hit home, hit that subscribe button because the next video is going to break down the exact negotiation script to use on your landlord at renewal line by line, including the three concession asks that land most often in 2026. The math has been lying to you. Time to start using it back.
script.analysis: Full 17767 canonical characters read. A rent-affordability explainer: renewal-letter hook, history of the 30% rule, Zillow typical rent vs renter incomes, JCHS cost burden, composite budgets (Kevin in Columbus, a Denver couple), RealPage algorithmic pricing and DOJ settlement, junk fees and the FTC rule, evictions, NLIHC housing wage, rent vs buy and mortgage amortisation, living with parents, seniors (Linda) and homelessness, the 2026 supply-driven softening and future tightening, and three actions. Verified: Zillow $1,910 and 1.8% growth, JCHS 22.6M/12.1M, RealPage settlement with no penalty. Reproduces: 30% income need, 45% burden, Kevin budget, eviction rate, first-year interest share. Problems: thumbnail $3,000 not in script; Denver -$938 not reproducible; FTC rule scope overstated; "five years ago essentially zero" down-payment claim; several statistics unfetched. The stored ending is complete.
